name: Chelsea Road Elm

location.address: Corner of Chelsea Road and Union Road, Nether Edge, Sheffield

access: Free. A street tree on the public pavement at a street corner, visible at any time.
transport: About 3 km south-west of Sheffield station. Buses from the city centre to Nether Edge stop within a few minutes' walk; check Travel South Yorkshire for the route.
story:
In 2017 people stood beneath this elm to keep the chainsaws off it. Sheffield's highways contract had marked it for felling, and what followed was a campaign of roughly four years. Protesters blocked the work, neighbours held a street party, and someone ran an open-top bus so people could see the butterflies in its crown.

The butterflies were the point. This is a Huntingdon elm, a hybrid of field and wych elm that has held out against Dutch elm disease, and it is one of something like a thousand mature elms left in the UK outside the strongholds of Brighton and Edinburgh. Elms are where the white-letter hairstreak lays its eggs, and Butterfly Conservation put out a statement on this tree's behalf. The Woodland Trust's Tree of the Year voters made it runner-up in 2016, and it was shortlisted again in 2023.

In 2019 the tree was saved, and young New Horizon elms were planted nearby to give the butterflies somewhere to go next. Local campaigners put the elm at about 120 years old in 2016 and 2017; a newspaper said 128 in 2023. Either way, it has outlasted the contract that wanted it gone.

The newest sighting we can point to is that 2023 shortlist. One unconfirmed report says the tree carries Dutch elm disease. If you pass the corner, tell us how it looks.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the large elm on the street corner, with young elms planted nearby. It stands on the corner of Chelsea Road and Union Road in Nether Edge.

name: Vernon Oak
access: Free. A street tree on the public pavement, visible at any time.
transport: Dore and Totley station is roughly a kilometre away, on the Sheffield to Manchester line; buses from Sheffield city centre serve Dore.
story:
Vernon Road in Dore is said to have only one tree, and in October 2017 a protester climbed it to stop it being cut down. The oak was on Sheffield's felling list under the city's street tree contract, and the fight over it reached the national press. The TV presenter Vernon Kay, whose name it happens to share, backed the campaign.

It was here first. The oak began as a field boundary tree, standing in farmland before the suburb grew up around it, which is why it now sits in the pavement of a residential road. Trees for Cities, writing in December 2018, called it about 150 years old and one of the most celebrated trees in Sheffield, and listed it among those the council agreed to keep after it reversed course that year. An independent panel of tree experts reportedly described it as a very fine specimen in excellent condition, with another 150 years of life ahead.

One honest gap. The sources call it an oak and nothing more precise, so we have not established which species. Most big oaks in this part of Yorkshire are pedunculate oaks, but that is a guess, and if you can tell from the leaves or the acorns, let us know.

The last firm news of it is the decision to keep it, in 2018. The exact spot along the road is not pinned either, so look for the single large oak in the pavement.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the single large oak growing in the pavement, reportedly the only tree on the road. It stands somewhere along Vernon Road in Dore; the pin marks the middle of the road.
